translation: O lord Nandīśa, O lord of all beings, O spotless one, O higher than the highest!
By what means, O lord of the gods, may one obtain the state of the spotless?
Reveal the prescription of samaya-conduct and the sādhana!
All that I wish to hear, for the welfare of practitioners.
O Mahādeva, swearing an oath to me, reveal the great Yoni!

sanskrit: vedānāṃ sāragamyañca taṃ sāraṃ me prakāśaya || 1/6 ||
translation: And reveal to me that essence — the means by which the essence of the Vedas is reached!
O goddess, it is more essential than the essence and higher than the highest — the highest of the high!

sanskrit: satyaṃ satyaṃ punaḥ satyaṃ satyaṃ satyaṃ punaḥ punaḥ || 1/8 ||
translation: Truth, truth, again truth — truth, truth, truth, again and again!

sanskrit: idantu paramaṃ guhyaṃ triṣu lokeṣu durlabham || 1/9 ||
translation: But this supreme secret is hard to obtain in the three worlds!
Even in a thousand successive births it cannot be told at all.
It must be concealed, concealed, concealed by you, again and again!

sanskrit: mantrārthaṃ mantracaitanyaṃ yonimudrāṃ na vetti yaḥ || 1/12 ||
translation: Whoever does not know the meaning of the mantra, the consciousness of the mantra, and the yoni-mudrā...
I will tell the great mantra — the meaning-essence of the mantra — O Sūreśvarī!
Only by purity of disposition, O beloved of the vital breath, is the mantra's meaning realized.

sanskrit: kālī tārā mahādevi bhuvaneśī ca ṣoḍaśī || 1/15 ||
translation: Kālī, Tārā — O great goddess — Bhuvaneśī and Ṣoḍaśī...

sanskrit: vagalā caiva mātaṅgī kamalā ca prakīrtitā || 1/16 ||
translation: And Vagalā, Mātaṅgī, and Kamalā are proclaimed.
Granting enjoyment, she is liberation — the goddess concealed by a crore of world-eggs.
She whose essence is the life-breath of the God of gods, she whose form is all the gods.
The goddess who effects creation and preservation, having Viṣṇu's form, the great sovereign.
By the mere hearing of this, the practitioner becomes liberated while living.

sanskrit: tat śrutvā pitaraḥ sarve nṛtyanti hṛṣṭamānasāḥ || 1/21 ||
translation: Having heard that, all the ancestors dance with joyful minds.
The great Vidyā, though not to be given freely, grants complete fruit in the Kali age.
In the Kali age, the wise one should worship the gods by the rule stated in the Āgama.
Kālikā, granting liberation, O goddess, grants swift fruit in the Kali age.

sanskrit: brahmāṇī kurute sṛṣṭiṃ na tu brahmā kadācana || 1/25 ||
translation: Brahmāṇī performs creation; Brahmā never does.

sanskrit: pālanaṃ vaiṣṇavī devi na tu viṣṇuḥ kadācana || 1/26 ||
translation: Vaiṣṇavī performs preservation, O goddess; Viṣṇu never does.

sanskrit: rudrāṇī kurute grāsaṃ na tu rudraḥ kadācana || 1/27 ||
translation: Rudrāṇī performs the devouring; Rudra never does.
The gods beginning with Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśa are proclaimed inert.
Because of her, the best of practitioners performs dharma, adharma, and the like.
And it is to be done according to the rule of the tradition, O Maheśvarī!

sanskrit: yā tu kṛṣṇā saiva kṛṣṇastathā brahmā prakīrtitaḥ || 1/31 ||
translation: She who is the dark one — she indeed is Kṛṣṇa; and so too Brahmā is proclaimed as such.
Whosoever, however, thinks of them as separate — that foolish-minded one is a sinner.
Whosoever thinks of them as non-different is a yogin; here there is no doubt.
With the delight of the flute's sound she bewitches the entire world.
In the Kali age, having attained blackness, she — though white — is of dark-blue form.

sanskrit: p. 2) tārakatvāt sadā tārā tāriṇīti prakīrtitā || 1/36 ||
translation: Because of her delivering power, she is always proclaimed Tārā, the crossing one.
The goddess who effects creation and preservation is also called Bhuvaneśī.
And the great goddess, without qualities, is celebrated as Ṣoḍaśī.
And the consort of Kālabhairava is celebrated as Bhairavī.

sanskrit: triguṇā ca mahādevī mohinī mokṣadā dhruvam || 1/40 ||
translation: And the great goddess, possessing the three guṇas, is Mohinī, granting liberation — certainly.
The great goddess, whose form is smoke, grants the four aims.

sanskrit: vakāre vāruṇī devī gakāre siddhidā smṛtā || 1/42 ||
translation: In the letter va resides the goddess Vāruṇī; in the letter ga she is known as granting siddhi.
Mātaṅgī, through her nature of intoxication, is the destroyer of the demon Mataṅga.
And the goddess dwelling in Vaikuṇṭha is proclaimed Kamalā.
These ten are the great Vidyās; and she is called the Siddha-vidyā.
In whatsoever manner, in the Kali age she grants complete fruit.

sanskrit: pāṣaṇḍe ca śaṭhe caiva nirguṇe caiva nindake || 1/47 ||
translation: Not to be revealed to a heretic, to a rogue, to one devoid of qualities, and to a reviler.

sanskrit: na prakāśyamidaṃ bhadre śapathaṃ me dhruvaṃ sadā || 1/48 ||
translation: This is not to be revealed, O blessed one; my oath is firm always.

sanskrit: āsāñcaiva samā nāsti nāsti tribhuvane dhruvam || 1/49 ||
translation: Of them there is no equal — none in the three worlds, certainly.
By mere recollection, O mistress of the gods, one is released from the bondage of existence.
And indeed from the qualityless, three bindus have arisen.
There was the bindu; from it the nāda; from the nāda, the arising of Śakti.
And from the nāda, O Maheśvarī, the half-bindu arose.
The goddess is without qualities and with qualities, having the form of Brahman, eternal.
The goddess, having consciousness as her form, illuminates all beings.

sanskrit: nirguṇā sā ca vijñeyā brahmarūpā ca kevalā || 1/56 ||
translation: And she is to be known as without qualities, having the form of Brahman, and alone.
Four-qualitied, O Maheśānī, having power over the four Vedas.
The great goddess, having all qualities, has power over the entire universe.
The mother of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva and the rest — O beauty of the gods!
The great goddess, one-qualitied, having the form of the single syllable.
But the great goddess, three-qualitied, is celebrated as three-syllabled.
Nine-qualitied, O Maheśānī, illuminating the nine syllables.
And indeed the twelve and the thirteen: the twelve-syllabled one, whose nature is the thirty-three (read: thirteen).
The goddess, consisting of fifteen syllables, illuminating the fifteen.
Endowed with the ten and the seven, she is proclaimed the seventeen-syllabled one.
Endowed with the twenty-eight syllables, having the form of the supremely worshipable.
Mantras exceeding twenty syllables are proclaimed the garland-mantras.
Proclaimed as twenty-three, twenty-four, and twenty-five.
Endowed with the group of twenty-eight, she is proclaimed twenty-eight.
Beginning with thirty and up to sixty-four syllables are proclaimed the long mantras.
And the mantras joined with svāhā are Śakti-mantras, O Pārvatī.
Thus ends the first chapter — in the Kubjikā Tantra, in the dialogue of Pārvatī and Parameśvara.

sanskrit: vinā yena na siddheta japapūjādikaṃ kvacit || 2/1 ||
translation: Without which, japa, worship, and the like would not be accomplished anywhere.

sanskrit: kakāraḥ kāmadaḥ prokto rephaḥ pāpasya nāśakaḥ || 2/2 || 2/
translation: The letter ka is declared to grant desires; the letter ra is the destroyer of sin.
The great goddess, having the form of nāda, without qualities, having the form of Brahman.
And the omkāra, having the form of Brahman — that one is both with qualities and without qualities.
And the letter ī, having the form of Durgā, grants the fruit of the four aims.
The letter ka is declared to be Varuṇa, the producer of the world's life-breath.
In the letter ī is the goddess Tāriṇī, who carries one across the ocean of existence.
This letter ra, having the form of fire, is the burner of the suffering of existence.
And when the goddess is with qualities, she grants all siddhis.
The god who grants liberation and nirvāṇa, granting all siddhis.
In the letter u is the goddess Bhairavī, destroying all dangers.
And in the letter ha is the great Viṣṇu, the destroyer of great sins.
In the letter u is the goddess Mohinī, who bewitches the world.

sanskrit: sadāśivo hakāraḥ syādukāre brahma caiva hi || 2/14 ||
translation: Sadāśiva is the letter ha; and indeed Brahmā is in the letter u.
By the mere recollection of this, one would obtain the merit of ten thousand horse-sacrifices.
In the letter ī is the supreme goddess, always consisting of the three guṇas.
The letter kṣa, granting the field, is Viṣṇu, the destroyer of great sins.
In the letter la is the goddess Caṇḍikā, destroying the demon Caṇḍa.
In the letter ka the earth is declared, with its mountains, forests, and groves.
In the letter la is the earth, O goddess, granting the fruit of the gift of land.
In the letter ka is Sundarī, O goddess; in the letter e, she has the form of the yoni.

sanskrit: parā ca paramā caiva paramātmakalā punaḥ || 2/22 ||
translation: And Parā, and indeed Paramā, and again the kalā of the supreme self.

sanskrit: kakāre ca mahādevo brahmāṇī repha eva ca || 2/23 ||
translation: And in the letter ka is Mahādeva; and indeed Brahmāṇī is the letter ra.
The letter ī — granting desires, lovely, adorned with nāda and bindu.
The letter u is the goddess Ṣoḍaśī; the letter ū is Bhuvaneśvarī.
The letter ha is Yoganidrā; and the letter ha is the supreme, all-pervading lord.
And indeed the letter ra, O great goddess, is adorned with nāda and bindu.
The one-syllabled great Vidyā — the eternal knowledge of Brahman.
